$comment: Matic bust avatar — machine-readable manifest. Source of truth for the client's state map.
Derived from BUST AVATAR SPECIFICATION v7 · 2026.09.09. Do not hand-transcribe from the PDF.
State names are v7's verbatim, British spelling where v7 uses it (apologising).
Every colour is a CSS custom property name, never a literal — see tokens{} for values.
$comment_shapes: eyeShapes and mouthShapes are the id suffixes present in the chassis SVG: #eyes-oval, #mouth-narrow, etc.
All are in the markup at all times. Switching is a data-attribute change on #eyes / #mouth; nothing is inserted or removed.
'happy' is v7's 'arc-up'. The shape id is 'happy'; use that in code and reserve 'arc-up' for prose.

crop.$comment: The head crop is a FIXED source box. It clips identically at every head-crop size — there is no size threshold.
crop.belowFloor: Do not render the avatar. Use the tray status dot.

rule.$comment: A state whose only differentiator is a fullBustOnly accessory is a full-bust state. That is escalating — see states.escalating.minSize.

trayReads.$comment: Four reads, separated by motion first (hue is unreadable at 16px on an unknown taskbar background). See reducedMotion.tray for the static fallback.

resting.meaning: Present and available, asking for nothing.

working.meaning: Busy on the user's behalf; no action needed yet.

needsYou.meaning: The user must answer something before anything else happens.

unavailable.meaning: Not a request — a statement that the assistant cannot work.

none.meaning: Transient. Does not reach the tray; the tray returns to resting.

trayReads.rule: The ring is only ever for a state that needs an answer. If it fires when nothing does, it stops meaning anything.

idle.notes: Default. The resting mouth keeps a shallow upward curve, not a flat bar — a deliberate tone decision.

listening.separatedBy: The head tilt — rig motion, which survives the head crop. Its ear rings also keep 88%.
listening.notes: The only state with a head tilt.

thinking.separatedBy: The gaze shift — inside the face screen, so it survives the head crop.
thinking.notes: Gaze off-axis is the strongest signal that attention is elsewhere. The violet is reinforcement only.

speaking.notes: 'talk' is the fallback when no viseme stream is bound. With a stream, drive #mouth from phonemeToMouth instead and ignore this state's mouth value.

greeting.notes: No arm to wave. The nod is a two-beat that resolves back to rest rather than looping, so the panel does not fidget while the user reads.

success.notes: The one state that may auto-dismiss the panel, so also the one that must not be reused for a partial fix. Never reaches the tray.

apologising.notes: It tried and could not help — relational, not technical. No badge and no alarm hue, so it never depends on colour alone. Not error's vocabulary.

declining.notes: Nothing in the knowledge base covers the question, so it says so and offers a ticket. This is the product working correctly, not a failure. Must never read as sorry: eyes level, attentive rather than smiling, no bow. round+narrow is used by nothing else, so it holds where the ? badge is cropped. The copy must state plainly that nothing has been filed.
declining.priority: The most-seen state and the one to get most right — it fires at the moment the user's trust is most in play.

escalating.separatedBy: Nothing that survives the head crop. The ticket sits at 146,136 — outside the crop box, 46% visible — and the amber tip is hue, which is never a differentiator in this spec.
escalating.constraint: FULL BUST ONLY — 96px and up. Below that it renders identically to thinking. The client must refuse to render escalating under 96px; the reference implementation logs a console warning when the ticket is not actually visible.
escalating.notes: What happens after the user accepts the offer; follows declining or apologising rather than replacing either. The confirmation must state plainly that a ticket was raised and carry its number.

error.notes: A technical fault on our side — impersonal. Cross eyes read as more urgent than any arc regardless of hue. In the tray it is the one state that goes static: absence of motion says the assistant cannot work, a statement rather than a request.

accept.separatedBy: Only the ABSENCE of listening's head tilt — its chest aperture is 11% visible under the head crop. Legible but weak; prefer the full bust.
accept.notes: Consent is a distinct moment and gets a distinct state. The avatar HOSTS the ask, it does not author it: the consent text is rendered by the privileged half of the application and shown verbatim. The avatar must never generate, paraphrase or restate those words.

ingest.notes: PARKED — not in v1 and not counted as delivered. Ship it disabled or omit it, but keep it in the set: a call site is designed (screenshot attachment when raising a ticket, where the user picks a window or region, sees exactly what will be sent, and approves it per ticket). Would need its own pairing if it ships.

$comment: eSpeak-ng / Piper phonemes → mouth shape. ONE table: OVR is not an intermediate.
Piper phonemises through eSpeak-ng and emits phonemes, not OVR visemes. At six shapes they map straight.
Unrecognised input resolves to 'closed'. This table is indexed every few milliseconds — keep it a flat lookup.

ovrToMouth.$comment: Legacy OVR viseme ids, accepted at the API boundary only so a future cloud TTS can be swapped in without touching the visual layer. Not used by Piper. Note DD and kk were byte-identical in the original 15-viseme set.

motion.$comment: Every value the implementation needs. Properties are transform/opacity only — no layout, no filters, nothing that forces GPU compositing.

jitter.$comment: Multiply duration by 0.95 + random()*0.1, computed ONCE per mount and stable for its lifetime.

randomStartPhase.$comment: Negative animation-delay, also computed once per mount. Without it, two avatars on screen breathe in lockstep — an obvious tell that they are one asset rather than two agents.

nod.$comment: A two-beat that RESOLVES, then the state falls back to idle's breathe. Do not loop it.

talk.$comment: Fallback chatter only. When a viseme stream is bound this animation must be OFF and #mouth switched per phoneme instead.

composition.$comment: How motions compose with a mouth swap during speech — the case that must not stutter.
composition.rule: Rig motion and mouth swapping are on DIFFERENT elements and different properties. #rig animates transform; #mouth changes a data-attribute that toggles which child is visible. A phoneme swap therefore never restarts, interrupts or recalculates the rig animation.
composition.forbidden: Do not put the mouth swap on a CSS transition, and do not animate the mouth's own transform while swapping shapes — at phoneme rate a transition either lags the audio or is cut off mid-interpolation, which reads as a wobble rather than speech.

$comment: prefers-reduced-motion behaviour, per motion. This was NOT in v7 and is a design decision made here.
The structural problem: v7 makes motion the primary channel in the tray, where hue is unreadable at 16px.
With motion off, four tray reads would collapse into one dot. So the tray needs a STATIC vocabulary that still separates four reads — see tray{} below.

avatar.nod: Off. Hold the rest pose. Greeting still reads via its grin.
avatar.tilt: Off. Hold the rest pose. Listening still reads via round eyes + roundSmall mouth + ear rings.
avatar.bow: Off. Hold the rest pose. Apologising still reads via lowered eyes — the only state with them.
avatar.pulse: Off. Hold the tip at full opacity (1), not at its dimmest.
avatar.dot: Off. Show all three dots static at full opacity, so thinking keeps its accessory.
avatar.ring: Off. Show ONE static ring per ear pod at scale 1, opacity 0.85 — listening keeps a visible accessory in place of the pulse.
avatar.aperture: Off. Show the dashed hex static at opacity 0.9 — accept's ask stays visible.
avatar.ingest: Off. Show the document static at its 0.78 keyframe (mid-draw), so the state still reads.
avatar.scan: Off. Hide the scan line entirely — a static line across the face reads as damage, not scanning.
avatar.talk: Off. Hold the 'closed' mouth when idle-speaking. Viseme swaps KEEP RUNNING — see note.
avatar.$note_visemes: Lip-sync is informative, not decorative: it conveys that speech is happening and roughly what is being said. Reduced motion should not silence it. Keep phoneme-driven #mouth swaps; they are discrete state changes, not animation. Provide a separate app-level setting for users who want them off too.

tray.$comment: The hard part, and a design question rather than an engineering one. Four reads must survive with zero motion, at 16px, on an unknown background. Solved with static FORM — the one channel that is neither motion nor hue.

resting.spec: Ring only: 2px stroke in the state colour, transparent centre. Reads lightest — present, nothing pending.

working.spec: Filled circle, no stroke. Reads heavier than hollow: engaged.

needsYou.spec: Filled circle PLUS a concentric static ring at 1.9x with a 1.5px stroke. The static residue of the ring animation, so the vocabulary is consistent whether motion is on or off. Visually the heaviest — it is the only one that asks for something.

unavailable.spec: Filled circle with a horizontal bar knocked out through the centre (60% of the diameter, 2px, in the background colour). Reads as struck through — cannot work.

tray.rationale: hollow / solid / solid+halo / solid+notch are four distinct silhouettes at 16px and survive greyscale, so the set degrades on form rather than depending on hue as a fallback. Ordering by visual weight also preserves the motion version's urgency ranking.
tray.acceptanceTest: Render all four at 16px in greyscale with animation disabled. If any two are confusable, the fallback has failed.

tokens.$comment: Values are v7 §07. The SVG references these as var(--matic-avatar-*) with these as fallbacks. Light and dark are token sets on the same markup — no second asset.

darkOverrides.$comment: v7 §05: on a dark panel the circular field is knocked out entirely. Only these change; every other token is inherited from light, so state colour is identical across themes.

do: Let the circular field sit on a light ground, or knock it out entirely on a dark panel.
Hold one state until the underlying condition changes.
Let each mount keep its own idle jitter and start phase.
Keep escalating on the full bust, 96px and up.
dont: Do not recolour the helmet, ear pods or field — state lives in the tip, screen and mark only.
Do not rotate or mirror the bust.
Do not scale the full bust below 64px.
Do not put error on a failed fix — that is apologising. Do not put either on a decline — that is declining.
Do not place escalating below 96px; it renders as thinking.
Do not use the tray ring for anything that does not need an answer.
placement.clearspace: One quarter of the field diameter on all sides. The antenna sits inside the field and needs no separate allowance.
